newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday expressed disappointment over the acquittal of Mayor Honorato Galvez of San Ildefonso town and ordered legal experts in Malacanang palace to review the case. The mayor was acquitted of a murder charge. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Executive secretary Ruben Torres said on Wednesday the ruling Lakas-NUCD party will meet to discuss anew the party stand on proposals to amend the Constitution (MALAYA)
- Five kidnap gang suspects have been arrested in separate raids by the Presidential Anti-Crime Commission Task Force and the Philippine National Police. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Department of Foreign Affairs said it is waiting for a final report from the Malaysian government on the case of a Filipina domestic helper who accused her employer, a diplomat in Kuala Lumpur, of raping her. (MALAYA)

- The powerful appropriations committee of the House of Representatives on Wednesday endorsed for floor debates House Bill 8033, appropriating 476.2 billion pesos for government operations and development programmes in 1997. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Car sales for January to September continued its uptrend, reaching 65,421 units, an increase of 26 percent from the 51,788 units sold in the same period last year, the Chamber of Automotive Manufacturers of the Philippines said. (MALAYA)

- The government has started briefing diplomatic personnel on the latest economic issues in a bid to start a new kind of diplomacy so the Philippines can be promoted as a good investment destination, an official of the Department of Finance said. (MALAYA)

- The Philippine Central Bank is planning to issue a limited edition of Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gold commemorative coins to mark next month's historic meeting of world leaders in the Philippines. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Filipino owned Marilag Transport Systems Inc is allotting 969.6 million pesos to operate air-conditioned ferry boats along Pasig river, Laguna de bay and Manila Bay. the ferry will be an alternative to travelling by Manila's congested roads. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- After reaching fever pitch in August, investment acitivities of Philippine insurance companies slowed in September, the Insurance Commission reported. The investments dropped 75 percent to 358.23 million pesos in September from 1.439 billion pesos in the previous month. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- Months after Malacanang ordered rebidding for the country's air radar system project, London-based GEC-Marconi appears confident it will still be able to bag the 3.0 billion peso radar contract. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)
